mainTopic: Half-measures and wording in פיגול intentions: combining thoughts, eating by dogs or fire, and one olive-bulk shared by two people
overview: The גמרא first finishes an earlier discussion about whether, for רבי יהודה, a person's words count as one combined statement (כלל) or as separate statements (פרט). It gives two versions of how one question makes the other unnecessary. Next comes a case of three half-olive-bulk intentions: time, then place, then time again. רבא says the two time-halves join and the offering is פיגול. רב המנונא says the middle thought makes it עירוב מחשבות. Each brings a proof from the laws of impurity, and each proof is pushed aside. בר קפרא's teaching, reported in three versions by רב דימי, רבין and רב אשי, rules that a lone half-olive-bulk place-thought cannot stop a full olive-bulk of time-thought from making פיגול. רבי ינאי says a thought that dogs will eat the meat tomorrow is פיגול. רבי אמי challenges this from fire, and the גמרא answers that it depends on whether he used the language of eating or of burning. Finally, רב אשי asks about one olive-bulk eaten by two people, and אביי starts an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If 'An Olive-Bulk and an Olive-Bulk' Is One Statement, the Other Case Is Obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that if even 'כזית' 'וכזית' counts as one combined statement (כלל), there is no need to ask about 'כזית למחר בחוץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if 'an olive-bulk' and 'and an olive-bulk' is one general statement, is it necessary to ask about 'an olive-bulk tomorrow outside'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for one of the questions asked earlier. If the harder case is already treated as one combined statement, the easier case obviously is too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כזית וכזית' sounds like two separate statements, especially with the word 'and'. 'כזית למחר בחוץ' is one smooth phrase, so it is even more clearly one statement. So if the first counts as a כלל, asking about the second is pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (opens a 'now that X is true, surely Y' argument)
A general or combined statement, counted as one thought
Is it necessary to ask? (said when the answer is obvious)
An olive-bulk, the minimum amount for פיגול intent

phrases.english: Now, if 'an olive-bulk' 'and an olive-bulk' is a general statement,
phrases.notes: He means: one olive-bulk eaten after its time and one olive-bulk eaten outside its place, said as two pieces joined by 'and'.

phrases.english: is it necessary to ask about 'an olive-bulk tomorrow outside'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about how רבי יהודה treats combined intentions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to ask about 'כזית למחר בחוץ' if 'כזית וכזית' is already a כלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A stronger case answers the weaker one. If the more separated wording counts as one statement, the more joined wording surely does.

steps.title: Another Version: If 'Tomorrow Outside' Is Separate, the Other Case Is Obvious
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the argument runs the other way: if even 'כזית למחר בחוץ' counts as separate statements (פרט), then 'כזית כזית' surely does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: If 'an olive-bulk tomorrow outside' counts as separate statements, is it necessary to ask about 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way of putting the same kind of challenge, but in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the starting point is the case that sounds most combined. If even that is treated as separate (פרט), the case that sounds more separated, 'כזית כזית', is certainly separate too. Both versions make the same point: one of the two questions makes the other unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version (a second way the discussion was passed down)
Separate, detailed statements, each counted on its own

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions are not the same point said twice. They assume opposite things about רבי יהודה's view. Version 1 assumes even the split wording 'כזית וכזית' is one combined statement (כלל). Version 2 assumes even the smooth wording 'כזית למחר בחוץ' is separate statements (פרט). They share only the shape of the argument: one question makes the other unnecessary.

phrases.english: Another version:
if 'an olive-bulk tomorrow outside' is separate statements,
is it necessary to ask about 'an olive-bulk' 'an olive-bulk'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version of step 1's argument, reversing the direction of the logic.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to ask about 'כזית כזית' if 'כזית למחר בחוץ' is already a פרט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the most combined-sounding wording counts as separate, the less combined wording is surely separate too.

steps.title: Half for Time, Half for Place, Half for Time: Does It Become פיגול?
steps.stepSummary: A new case: a person intended half an olive-bulk beyond its time, half outside its place, and half beyond its time again. רבא says the two time-halves join and it is פיגול. רב המנונא says it is a mix of intentions (עירוב מחשבות).
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Half an olive-bulk beyond its time, half an olive-bulk outside its place, and half an olive-bulk beyond its time. רבא said: 'He awoke like one asleep': the פיגול. And רב המנונא said: It is a mixture of intentions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion with a dispute between two אמוראים. They argue whether a 'place' thought in the middle stops two 'time' halves from joining into פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each thought alone is only half the needed amount. רבא says the first time-thought 'wakes up' when the second time-half comes, so together they make a full olive-bulk of time intent, and the offering is פיגול. רב המנונא says the middle place-thought mixes in and interferes, so this is עירוב מחשבות and there is no פיגול (no כרת).

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond its time: intent to eat the offering after the allowed time; this makes פיגול
Outside its place: intent to eat it outside the allowed area; this makes it פסול but not פיגול
An offering ruined by improper intent about time; eating it brings כרת
Mixed intentions: time and place thoughts combined, so it is not pure פיגול

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides whether the offering brings כרת as פיגול or is only פסול. It also sets up a general question: can a small 'interrupting' thought break the joining of two halves?

phrases.english: It was stated: half an olive-bulk beyond its time,
half an olive-bulk outside its place,
and half an olive-bulk beyond its time –
Rava said: 'He awoke like one asleep': the piggul.
phrases.notes: תהלים 78:65. The first 'time' thought wakes up and joins the second one, so the half-thought in the middle doesn't count.

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna said:
It is a mixture of intentions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the כלל/פרט discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא: the two time-halves join and the offering is פיגול. רב המנונא: the middle place-thought makes it עירוב מחשבות, so it is not פיגול.

steps.title: רבא's Proof from Mixing Foods with Different Levels of Impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבא supports his view from a משנה: an egg-bulk of ראשון mixed with an egg-bulk of שני is ראשון; if split, each part is שני. So if they are mixed back together, they go back to being ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say this? As we learned: An egg-bulk of first-degree food and an egg-bulk of second-degree food that one mixed together are first-degree. If he divided them, this one is second-degree and that one is second-degree. So if he mixed them again, they are first-degree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source from a משנה to prove that something 'weakened' can come back to full strength when its parts are put back together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the mixture is split, each half has too little ראשון food, so it drops to שני. רבא reads the משנה as implying that remixing brings back ראשון status, even though each piece was 'downgraded' for a while. The same is true for פיגול: the first time-half was 'asleep' while the place-thought came between, and it 'wakes up' when the second time-half joins it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introduces a speaker's own proof)
An egg-bulk, the amount of food needed to pass on impurity
First-degree impurity
Second-degree impurity

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's model: parts that each became 'too small' can rejoin and get back their full status. That is why he says the two time-halves join into פיגול despite the place-thought in the middle.

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
As we learned: An egg-bulk of first-degree food
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in טהרות (1:5).

phrases.english: and an egg-bulk of second-degree food
that one mixed together – it is first-degree.
If he divided them – this is second-degree and that is second-degree.
This implies that if he mixed them again – it is first-degree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא supports his ruling from step 3 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that two half-thoughts of time rejoin into פיגול despite the interrupting place-thought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה טהרות 1:5: the mixture of ראשון and שני food drops to שני when split, and by רבא's inference goes back to ראשון when remixed.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the later part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows from the סיפא of the משנה that split pieces can go back to being ראשון once they come together again.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do I know they go back to being ראשון when joined? The later part of the משנה says: if each piece falls on its own onto a loaf of תרומה, it only makes the loaf unfit. If both fall together, they make the loaf שני.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up the claim from the last step, that the split pieces go back to being ראשון when they rejoin. His source is the later part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece on its own counts only as שני, so touching תרומה just makes it unfit. If both pieces touch together, the loaf becomes שני, which only a ראשון can cause. So the ראשון status was hidden while the pieces were apart and came back when they joined. רבא says the same is true for two halves of a time-intention: they join to make פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: the later part of a משנה
a loaf of תרומה
they made it unfit (but it cannot pass impurity on)
at the same time, together

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'unfit' with 'impure.' Making the loaf unfit (פסול) is weaker than making it שני. That difference is the whole proof.

phrases.english: From where do I know this?
From the fact that the latter clause teaches:
If this one fell by itself and that one fell by itself
onto a loaf of terumah, they disqualify it.
If they both fell at once, they make it second-degree.
phrases.notes: Only a ראשון can make something שני, so together the pieces must be acting as ראשון again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's proof from step 4 by showing where the משנה teaches that rejoined pieces become ראשון again.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that two half-כזית time-intentions join to make פיגול even with an outside-place intention between them.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה (two pieces falling together onto a loaf of תרומה make it שני).

steps.title: רב המנונא: impurity is different because there was a full measure
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says the impurity case does not prove anything about פיגול, because there a full egg-bulk existed from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא says: there, there was a full measure; here, there is no full measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא pushes aside רבא's proof by showing the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the impurity case, a whole כביצה of ראשון food existed at the start. It was only divided and then put back, so its strong status can come back. With the offering, the person never thought one full כזית of a time-intention all at once, so there is no full measure to bring back.

keyTerms.meaning: the required minimum amount (here an egg-bulk or an olive-bulk)
there (the impurity case)
here (the פיגול case)

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna says:
There, there is a measure,
phrases.notes: The ראשון food started as a full egg-bulk before it was split.

phrases.english: here, there is no measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר: הָתָם אִיכָּא שִׁיעוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from steps 4-5 by showing how impurity differs from פיגול.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. It does not argue with the impurity ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The impurity case started with a full measure that was split. The פיגול case never had a full measure of time-intention to bring back.

steps.title: רב המנונא's proof: mixed impurity joins at the lighter level
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא brings a משנה: food of first and second level join only at the lighter level, which seems to mean the stronger status does not come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: How do I know this? We learned: food made impure by a primary source and food made impure by a derivative join together, and they make things impure at the lighter level of the two. Doesn't that mean even when the full measure is made up again?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב המנונא brings his own proof from a different משנה, to show that the stronger status is lost once it is mixed in this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says ראשון food and שני food together make only a שני. רב המנונא reads this as covering even a case where the ראשון part was brought back to full size, and still it stays at the lighter level. If so, the lost ראשון status does not come back, and in the same way the outside-place intention blocks the time-halves from joining into פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: a primary source of impurity; food it touches becomes ראשון
a derivative of impurity; food it touches becomes שני
they join together to make up the measure
at the lighter (more lenient) level of the two
he filled it up again, brought it back to the full measure

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said: From where do I say it?
As we learned:
Food that became impure through a primary source of impurity,
and food that became impure through a derivative of impurity,
join with each other
to make impure at the lighter level of the two.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי, לָאו אַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲדַר מַלְּיֵיהּ?
phrases.english: What, is it not even where one made up the measure again?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having rejected רבא's proof, רב המנונא now offers a positive proof for his own view.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's ruling that the case is a mix of intentions (עירוב מחשבות) and not פיגול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה stating that food from an אב הטומאה and food from a ולד הטומאה join only at the lighter level.

steps.title: The proof is pushed aside: maybe the measure was not made up again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה may be talking only about a case where the full measure was not put back together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is talking about where one did not make up the measure again!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside רב המנונא's proof by reading the משנה as a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ראשון part was never brought back to a full egg-bulk, of course it can only work as a שני, and that tells us nothing new. So the משנה does not prove that a status which was there before is lost for good. Since רבא's proof was also pushed aside in step 6, neither side has been proven, and the dispute stays as it was.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps, maybe

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: pieces that came from a full measure can rejoin and bring back their stronger status (ראשון, and likewise פיגול). רב המנונא: impurity is different because a full measure existed at the start. His proof from the משנה is pushed aside, since it may be talking about a case where the measure was never made up again.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is where one did not make up the measure again!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב המנונא's proof from step 7 by reading the משנה as a narrower case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not prove רבא right or רב המנונא wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה covers a case where the full measure was made up again. The משנה may mean only a case where it was not.

steps.title: רב דימי's report: a half-olive-bulk 'place' thought does not block פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports בר קפרא's ruling. A half-olive-bulk thought of חוץ למקומו, followed by two half-olive-bulk thoughts of חוץ לזמנו, still makes the קרבן פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: if a person intended half an olive-bulk outside its place, then half an olive-bulk beyond its time, then another half beyond its time, בר קפרא teaches that it is פיגול. Half an olive-bulk does not take effect where there is a full olive-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching, carried by רב דימי, about thoughts that are each only half an olive-bulk. It fits the earlier discussion about half-measures joining together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two 'time' halves add up to a full olive-bulk, and a full olive-bulk of a 'time' thought is what makes פיגול. The single 'place' half is too small to count, so it cannot spoil the פיגול. This holds even though it came first.

keyTerms.meaning: Half an olive-bulk, which is less than the minimum size that counts
An intention to eat the קרבן outside its proper place
An intention to eat the קרבן after its proper time. This is the thought that makes פיגול
A קרבן ruined by a wrong-time intention

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the 'place' thought is being ignored completely. It is simply too small (only half) to block the full olive-bulk of 'time' thoughts from making פיגול.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
half an olive-bulk outside its place,
and half an olive-bulk beyond its time,
and half an olive-bulk beyond its time —
Bar Kappara teaches: it is piggul;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חֲצִי זַיִת מוֹעִיל בִּמְקוֹם כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk does not take effect where there is an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling about half-olive-bulk measures, continuing the theme of halves joining together.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Place-half, then time-half, then time-half: the קרבן is פיגול, because a half-olive-bulk thought cannot interfere with a full olive-bulk.

steps.title: Ravin's version: the same ruling with the order switched
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports בר קפרא's ruling with the two 'time' halves first and the 'place' half last. The result and the reason stay the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: half an olive-bulk beyond its time, half an olive-bulk beyond its time, and half an olive-bulk outside its place. בר קפרא teaches that it is פיגול, because half an olive-bulk does not take effect where there is a full olive-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same teaching, as רבין reported it. The thoughts come in a different order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the two 'time' halves come first and complete a full olive-bulk. Only then does the half 'place' thought come. The ruling is still פיגול, for the same reason: a half cannot interfere with a whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Where there is a full olive-bulk

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
half an olive-bulk beyond its time,
and half an olive-bulk beyond its time,
and half an olive-bulk outside its place —
Bar Kappara teaches: it is piggul;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חֲצִי זַיִת מוֹעִיל בִּמְקוֹם כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk does not take effect where there is an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second report of בר קפרא's teaching, with the order of the thoughts reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Time-half, time-half, then place-half: the קרבן is פיגול.

steps.title: רב אשי's version: a half and a mixed full olive-bulk
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches the case another way. A half-olive-bulk 'time' thought comes first, then one olive-bulk split between 'place' and 'time'. It is still פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי teaches it like this: half an olive-bulk beyond its time, and then an olive-bulk, half of it outside its place and half of it beyond its time. בר קפרא teaches that it is פיגול, because half an olive-bulk does not take effect where there is a full olive-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third way of phrasing בר קפרא's case, in the name of רב אשי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the second thought is about one full olive-bulk, split down the middle between 'place' and 'time'. The 'time' half inside it joins the first 'time' half to make a full olive-bulk. The 'place' half is too small to block it, so the ruling stays פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it like this, giving his own wording of the teaching
Half of it

steps.whatToRemember: All three versions agree: two 'time' halves join to make a full olive-bulk and cause פיגול, and a lone half-olive-bulk 'place' thought cannot stop it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi teaches it like this:
half an olive-bulk beyond its time,
and an olive-bulk — half of it outside its place
and half of it beyond its time;
Bar Kappara teaches: it is piggul;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חֲצִי זַיִת מוֹעִיל בִּמְקוֹם כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk does not take effect where there is an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third wording of the same teaching, with the second thought framed as one mixed olive-bulk.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Time-half, then one olive-bulk split between place and time: the קרבן is פיגול.

steps.title: Intending that dogs eat the קרבן the next day
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי rules that thinking that dogs will eat the קרבן tomorrow makes it פיגול. He proves that dogs eating counts as 'eating' from a פסוק about איזבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי says: if a person intended that dogs would eat it tomorrow, it is פיגול, as it is written: 'And the dogs shall eat איזבל in the portion of יזרעאל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching. רבי ינאי says that a wrong-time thought about dogs eating the meat also makes פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול normally comes from a thought about 'eating' the קרבן at the wrong time. One might think only people eating counts. רבי ינאי shows from the פסוק that the תנ"ך calls what dogs do 'eating', so this thought counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended, or had in mind
Dogs
Tomorrow, after the proper time
Queen איזבל, wife of אחאב

steps.whyThisMatters: It widens the meaning of 'eating' in the rules of פיגול to include animals eating, not just people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says:
if he intended that dogs would eat it tomorrow —
it is piggul; as it is written:
"And the dogs shall eat Jezebel
in the portion of Jezreel."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the half-measure cases to a new question: what kind of 'eating' counts for פיגול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thought that dogs will eat the קרבן the next day makes it פיגול, since a dog eating is called 'eating' in the פסוק.

steps.title: If dogs count as eating, does fire count too?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי argues that רבי ינאי's reasoning would make a thought that fire will consume the קרבן tomorrow into פיגול. That seems to clash with a משנה saying eating and burning do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי objected: If so, then if someone thought that a fire would consume the קרבן tomorrow, it should also be פיגול, since a פסוק says 'a fire not blown shall consume (literally: eat) him.' And if you say that is right, a משנה teaches: if he thought to eat half an olive-bulk and burn half an olive-bulk, the קרבן is fit, because eating and burning do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes רבי ינאי's dog proof one step further, to fire. He shows that this seems to contradict a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי said dogs eating counts as 'eating' because a פסוק uses that word. By the same logic, fire burning should count as 'eating', because a פסוק says fire 'eats.' But the משנה says a burning-thought and an eating-thought do not combine, so burning must not be the same as eating.

keyTerms.meaning: He objected to it; a strong challenge against a statement
But if that is so; it introduces an unwanted result of the earlier logic
Burning on the altar
Join together to make a full measure

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami objected to it:
But if that is so,
if he intended that fire would consume it tomorrow,
as it is written: "A fire not blown shall consume him"
phrases.notes: איוב 20:26. 'Consume' here literally means 'eat', just like in the פסוק about the dogs.

phrases.english: would it also be פיגול?!
And if you say, yes, it is so,
but didn't we learn in the משנה:
to eat half an olive-bulk
and to burn half an olive-bulk: it is fit,
because eating and burning do not join together!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי ינאי's proof from the פסוק about איזבל by extending it to fire.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's rule that any 'eating' the פסוק calls eating, such as by dogs, counts for פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a פסוק's use of 'eating' is enough, fire also 'eats'. Then a burning-thought should combine with an eating-thought. But the משנה says they do not combine.

steps.title: It depends on the words he used
steps.stepSummary: If he expressed the fire-thought using the word 'eating', it does count as eating. The משנה is about someone who used the word 'burning', and that is a separate category.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said it in the language of eating, then yes, it counts. The משנה is talking about where he said it in the language of burning. The language of eating is one thing, and the language of burning is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי אמי. What matters is the wording the person used in his thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who thinks 'fire will eat it tomorrow' has used eating language, so it is indeed פיגול, just as רבי ינאי said. The משנה's case is someone who thought 'to burn', and burning language is a different category. So it does not join with eating.

keyTerms.meaning: He expressed it; the words he actually used
In the language of; using the wording of
What case are we dealing with here? It narrows down the case
Separate, on its own

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּאַפְּקַהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲכִילָה – הָכִי נָמֵי;
phrases.english: If he expressed it in the language of eating, then indeed so;
here, what case are we dealing with?
Where he expressed it in the language of burning.
For the language of eating is separate,
and the language of burning is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאַפְּקַהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן אֲכִילָה – הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אמי's challenge and keeps רבי ינאי's rule standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה by the wording used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a פסוק calls fire's consuming 'eating', any thought about fire consuming the קרבן should count as eating. Then the משנה's eating-half and burning-half should join together.
steps.terutzMaskana: It depends on his words. A thought worded as 'eating', even by fire, counts as eating. A thought worded as 'burning' is a separate category and does not combine with eating.
steps.whatToRemember: In פיגול thoughts, the wording counts. 'Eating' language and 'burning' language are two separate categories, even when fire is involved.

steps.title: One olive-bulk shared by two people
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about a thought that two people will eat one olive-bulk together. Do we follow the total thought, which is a full olive-bulk? Or do we follow each eater, who eats less than an olive-bulk?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If he thought that two people would eat one olive-bulk, what is the law? Do we follow the thought, and there is a full measure? Or do we follow the eaters, and neither has a full measure?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי opens a new question about the minimum amount for a פיגול thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פיגול thought needs at least an olive-bulk. Here the thought covers a full olive-bulk, but it is split between two people, so each one eats only half. The question is whether we measure the thought as a whole or measure what each person eats.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked; he raised an open question
What is the law?
Do we follow the thought?
The required measure
The eaters

phrases.english: רב אשי asked:
If he intended that an olive-bulk be eaten
by two people, what is the law?
Do we follow the thought,
and there is a full measure,
or do we follow the eaters,
and there is no full measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how to measure the olive-bulk in a פיגול thought.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the olive-bulk minimum measured by the total thought, or by what each eater eats?

steps.title: אביי brings the eating-and-burning משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins answering רב אשי's question by quoting the משנה about half an olive-bulk eaten and half burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Come and hear: If he thought to eat half an olive-bulk and to burn half an olive-bulk, the קרבן is fit, because eating and burning do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a משנה as the start of an answer to רב אשי. This step sets up the proof, and the גמרא explains how it proves anything on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a specific reason why the halves do not combine: one half is eating and the other is burning. אביי seems to be pointing at that reason as a hint toward an answer for the two-people case, which the גמרא develops next.

phrases.english: אביי said: Come and hear:
to eat half an olive-bulk
and to burn half an olive-bulk: it is fit,
because eating and burning do not join together.
phrases.notes: This is the same משנה רבי אמי quoted above, now used for רב אשי's question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempted answer to רב אשי's question.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's question about one olive-bulk eaten by two people
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: half an olive-bulk to eat and half to burn is fit, because eating and burning do not join together.
